title: The Decline and Revival of Madagascar's Cinema Halls
description: At independence, Madagascar had a functioning network of cinema halls concentrated in Antananarivo and the coastal cities. In the decades that followed, political instability, economic deterioration, and the spread of VHS and informal video circulation eroded theatrical audiences. Many of the country's historic cinema buildings were converted to churches, warehouses, or other uses. By the 1990s, formal cinema infrastructure had largely collapsed. A slow revival began around 2006 with the founding of Rencontres du Film Court Madagascar — the country's first dedicated film festival — and continued with the establishment of the Cinépax network, which has restored theatrical distribution in the 2020s.
